name: Daniel
label: Premium payer angry about podcast ads
who: I use Spotify to listen to podcasts every single day and I have paid for Premium for years. I expect Premium to mean no ads, so I get angry when Spotify's own ads interrupt the shows I listen to.
value_for_money: They feel they pay a lot for Premium ([16]) and that paying 'a stupid amount' should mean no ads ([35]); one podcast subscription they pay for costs $5.99 a month for no ads ([32]). They accept creator-placed sponsor reads and say podcasters need to get paid ([36], [39]), so their objection is to Spotify-inserted ads on a paid plan.
loyalty: They stay because of years of Premium tenure and saved podcast content ([17], [33]), and they say they still like the app overall ([14]). What would make them leave is ads on Premium: some have already stopped using Spotify for podcasts and moved to Apple Podcasts, Deezer or Pocket Casts ([22], [24], [30]), and others say they will delete their account if they hear one more ad ([14]).
pain_points: Unskippable Spotify ads inserted into podcasts on Premium
Ads cut episodes off mid-sentence and play much louder than the show
Premium is seen as music-only, so podcast ads feel like a broken promise
Three or four ads in a row before the episode starts
likes: Creator-placed sponsor reads they can tolerate
Podcasters getting paid for their work
Years of saved podcast content on Spotify
reasons_to_stay: They value a long-standing Premium relationship and the content they have saved in the app ([17], [33]). Several say they like Spotify overall and object specifically to the ads it inserts into podcasts ([14], [35]), so the complaint is about one feature rather than the whole service.
tone: Blunt, angry and often profane, with short rants and occasional questions aimed at other users.
